# `nlink-lab ps`

The background processes `spawn` started, alive and exited (exited ones stay until the lab is destroyed, with their exit code). `ps NODE` shows one node's; `-q` prints only PIDs.

```bash
nlink-lab ps
nlink-lab ps server --alive-only
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
List background processes (alive and exited) tracked by `spawn`.

Exited processes remain in the listing with `alive: false` so post-mortem inspection (which log files? when did they exit?) is possible. They are pruned only when the lab is destroyed. Consumers polling "is X still running?" must check the `alive` field, not just look up the PID — or pass `--alive-only` to filter dead entries out at the source.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): { "schema_version": 2, "lab": str, "processes": [ { "node": str, "pid": int, "host_pid": int, "alive": bool, "exit_code": int | null, "stdout_log": str | null, "stderr_log": str | null }, ... ] } Schema: docs/json-schemas/ps.schema.json. With `--quiet`, the PIDs, one per line.

Usage: nlink-lab ps [OPTIONS] [NODE]

Arguments:
  [NODE]
          Only this node's processes

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

      --alive-only
          Hide processes whose tracked PID has exited (alive == false). Useful for "is X still running?" polling loops where exited post-mortem entries would otherwise be misread as alive

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
